title: Distributed compact serializer and ordered queue proxy for real-time console metrics
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: The current console metrics pipeline emits verbose JSON messages per event which inflate network egress, increase downstream deserialization overhead, and exacerbate hotkey amplification for high-cardinality tenants. Ordering guarantees are currently coarse-grained (per-partition) which leads to reordering in several downstream enrichers and causes spikes in tail latency when replaying for backfills.

Proposed solution: Implement a two-part runtime feature: (1) a compact binary serializer for telemetry events and (2) an ordered queue proxy that enforces per-tenant soft ordering while remaining spill-to-disk resilient. The serializer will use a compact, schema-evolving encoding (varint fields, delta timestamp, small-string dictionary for high-frequency keys, optional zstd for large payloads) to reduce message size and CPU cost. The queue proxy will sit between the ingress gateway and the existing stream processors; it provides small, shard-local ordered windows using sequence numbers and idempotency tokens to enable downstream exactly-once semantics without global coordination.

Goals and success criteria: Reduce average event size by >= 3x, reduce network bytes for ingest by >= 60%, maintain p99 end-to-end latency < 350ms for 95% of tenants under normal load, and eliminate reordering-caused duplicates in downstream enrichment flows. Support tenant isolation: a misbehaving tenant should be able to be rate-limited or evicted without violating ordering guarantees for other tenants.

Design highlights: 
- Serializer format: schema v1 with field tags and varint encoding. Use a small per-shard dictionary for strings common in keys/labels, refreshed every 10s. Provide adapters to produce and consume the format in SDKs (Go/Node/Python).
- Queue proxy: lock-free ring buffer per-shard with admission control (token-bucket per-tenant), local sequencing, and synchronous local checkpointing. In case of spill, messages are flushed to per-shard append-only files with checksummed segments. On restart, proxies replay based on sequence numbers; downstream dedup uses idempotency tokens.
- Backpressure: queue proxy exposes a control plane endpoint for the ingress to receive explicit backpressure signals and a passive telemetry stream for capacity metrics. We will integrate with the existing ingress token-limiters to short-circuit expensive serializations when under pressure.
- Observability: metrics for serialized_bytes, compression_ratio, per-tenant queue_depth, p50/p95/p99 latency to processor, reorder_events, spilled_segments_count. Tracing will annotate sequence numbers for cross-service correlation.

Trade-offs considered: Strong global ordering was rejected due to coordination overhead and tail latency impact. We intentionally accept soft ordering windows (configurable window size) to balance throughput vs strictness. There is additional complexity in schema evolution and SDK adapters; we mitigate with thorough compatibility tests and version negotiation headers.

Rollout plan: 
1) Implement serializer library and unit tests; provide binary format spec and SDK adapters (internal alpha) — 2 sprints.
2) Deploy queue proxy as an opt-in feature behind a feature flag in a single region with synthetic traffic and a small group of low-risk tenants; run for 2 weeks.
3) Enable for high-volume tenants with monitoring and automated rollback hooks.
4) Gradual regional rollout with canarying and observability dashboards.

Monitoring and post-deploy checks: dashboard with bytes/sec saved, compression ratio, p50/p95/p99 latency, reorder count, spill-to-disk rate, and consumer ack lag. Set automated alerts for reorder_events > 1% for > 10m, spill_rate > 0.1% sustained, or sustained p99 > 500ms.

Related artifacts: design doc (Confluence), serializer spec, integration test harness in repo infra/ingest-tests, and a staging PR for SDK adapters.

Notes: This ticket focuses on the runtime components; separate tickets will track SDK rollout, legal/compression policy review, and long-term storage format migration.
comments: 2026-02-02 - Ava Martinez: Initial ticket created after spike showing 2.8x network overhead on top 10 tenants. Attached serializer sketch and initial microbenchmarks (local).

2026-02-10 - Liam O'Connor: Completed prototype for varint encoding and per-shard dictionary. Observed 3.6x reduction on synthetic traces. Found edge case with empty-label heavy events increasing CPU on encode; added fast-path for empty labels.

2026-02-18 - Priya Kapoor (review): Design looks strong. Flagging that KMS integration for optional zstd-compressed payloads needs security review; recommend toggling compression per-tenant. Also request for explicit GC safety for spill files.

2026-02-24 - Liam O'Connor: Addressed security note; compression toggles added and documented. Implemented checksum for spill segments and a safe-replay unit test. Added per-tenant token-bucket admission and adjustable window-size config.

2026-03-03 - SRE/Oncall (feedback): Ran a 6-hour soak with canary tenant. Observed occasional spike in p99 during heavy orchestration events; traced to snapshot flush blocking the ring buffer allocation. Plan: make snapshot flush async with bounded concurrency.
2026-03-08 - Ava Martinez: Async snapshot flush implemented, updated tests. Starting staged canary for region eu-west-1 with 5 production tenants tomorrow. Marking readiness for infra review.
2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Infra review completed. No major blockers. Updating ticket status to In Progress and bumping estimate artifacts to include SDK release tasks.
